headline: Resolution to reduce heavy trucking on neighborhood streets kept in committee and referred to Traffic Commission and DPW.
summary: Resolution 25-095 was offered by Justin Tseng and Anna Callahan. A presentation said state approval from MassDOT is generally needed for a heavy truck exclusion on trucks rated above 10,000 pounds, plus an engineering study. The Traffic Commission and DPW were asked for a response by January 31st, with further discussion at a meeting in the new year.
decisions: Kept resolution 25-095 in committee and referred it to the Traffic Commission and DPW, 5-0 on roll call.
discussion: Heavy truck rules: A presentation said MassDOT approval is generally needed before a heavy truck exclusion, for trucks rated above 10,000 pounds. An engineering study is also required, covering vehicle counts, alternate routes, road width, and nearby schools.

Study cost: Members suggested getting a cost estimate from DPW for an outside engineering study. Members also asked the Traffic Commission for a list of existing exclusions and past requests that were denied.
Traffic shifting: Members warned that moving traffic from one street can push it onto another. Private ways were raised as a concern, since residents pay to maintain them.
Named streets: Harvard Street, Bonner, and Alexander were named as streets with cut-through heavy truck traffic.
Next steps: Members agreed to bring in the Traffic Commission, Police Department, and DPW, and to hear from residents at a later meeting.

decision_evidence.quote: I'd make a motion that we keep the paper in committee and refer your document out to the traffic commission and DPW request a response by January 31st and further meeting in the new year. ... Councillor Scarpelli. Yes. Chair Callahan. Yes.

decision_titles: Resolution 25-095 on reducing heavy trucking on neighborhood streets
